title: performance: canary auto-detect regression thresholds and hysteresis rollout guards
author: Morgan Chen
description: Motivation: reduce noisy canary failures and rollbacks caused by transient latency/throughput spikes and narrow sample sizes. This change implements adaptive regression detection thresholds and a hysteresis-based rollout guard for performance canaries. Key behaviors: 1) dynamic thresholding - compute expected latency/throughput baselines per-route and per-model using an exponentially weighted moving average and scale detection thresholds by observed variance; 2) hysteresis windowing - require a sustained regression over a configurable time window and a minimum number of affected requests before failing a canary; 3) staged reaction policy - when a regression is detected, the guard can either throttle traffic, mark the canary as degraded (soft-fail) for manual inspection, or abort the rollout (hard-fail) depending on severity; 4) tighter integration with rollout automation - the guard emits structured signals consumed by the rollout controller so canary traffic can be automatically rolled back or limited; 5) observability - new metrics + dashboard panels and tracing attributes to make regressions actionable. This PR contains implementation, unit and integration tests, Canary e2e harness updates, and docs for the configuration knobs. See linked Linear items for design notes and thresholds. Testing: local e2e and perf-canary lab run with synthetic noise patterns. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous pass/fail behavior unless the hysteresis window or adaptive thresholds are enabled via config. Checklist: - [x] Design doc in ENG-1248 - [x] Core detection algorithm implemented - [x] Unit tests for statistical detection and hysteresis - [x] Canary e2e updated in perf-canary harness - [x] Dashboard/Alert updates in console - [x] Docs updated for rollout guard knobs
